title: Grimaud between Port Grimaud, the plain and water landscapes
author: Caramagnols
excerpt: In Grimaud, the descent towards the plain and Port Grimaud changes the walk completely. Stone lanes give way to canals, wet sectors and another relation to the gulf.
content:
Grimaud brings together two readings that are too often separated: the old hill village and the lower opening towards the plain and Port Grimaud. Yet this continuity is exactly what makes the commune distinctive.

From height down to the plain

As one descends from the village, the landscape loosens. Lines become longer, water grows more present and the commune shows uses that are more open, first agricultural and then more openly harbour-related.

Port Grimaud as another face of the commune

Port Grimaud does not replace the old village; it extends it in a very different way. Canals, water circulation and moorings give the walk a vocabulary almost opposite to that of the old streets.

Why the contrast still holds together

What might look scattered in fact holds together through geography. Relief, plain, water and sea follow one another within the same commune. This passage from one world to another is what makes Grimaud especially interesting.

This note extends the page Walking Through Grimaud. To continue within the same cluster, it also helps to open Grimaud, castle, lanes and hill village.
